title: Patchogue
summary: Patchogue is a Brookhaven placename connected with Pochoug Neck, local stream geography, and later village history on the south shore of Long Island.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Patchogue village point based on Tooker location; not an exact historical Pochoug Neck or stream coordinate.
introduction_content: Patchogue is connected with the western part of Brookhaven and with earlier forms such as Pochoug, Pochog, and Patchague.
history_content: The placename is tied to Pochoug Neck and to later explanations of local stream geography. Dated details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as a turning place or where they divide in two, referring to a landscape where streams came together or separated. Related forms and comparisons include Pochoug, Pauchogue, and the Massachusetts form Pohshdog. Earlier claims that it referred to a separate Pochaug tribe or meant a place of many streams need careful review against source evidence.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names hold significance beyond mere geographical labels; they embody a vibrant tradition that ties communities to their environment.”

— Ellen Kathrine Bludd and Karine Nigar Aarskog, Why is it important to use Sami place names? (2026), opening statement
whereintheworld_content: Approximate/general point at modern Patchogue village in the Town of Brookhaven. This marker is not an exact historical Pochoug Neck, deed, or stream-boundary coordinate.
